text:
maya: quick heads-up — rolled out the auto-prefix KV cache + adaptive (seq-aware) batching to canary (10%) at 13:02 PT. initial numbers look promising. :sparkles:

deploy-bot: deploy release/auto-prefix-cache-adaptive-batcher -> canary cluster completed (id: depl_20260322_17)

maya: short summary from the canary slice: p50 latency down ~230ms -> ~120ms for typical short prompts, p95 down ~560ms -> ~340ms, tokens/sec up ~22%. estimated cost/token -18% based on recent billing sampling.

aj: wow nice! do you have a link to the dashboard or the query?

maya: posted the graphs: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/abc123/auto-cache-batcher (canary vs baseline). query is ordinary request_latency{route="text.generate"}.

david: any regressions for long-context workloads? we changed cache behavior, right?

maya: TTLs unchanged. change is about smarter prefix matching + not batching long sequences with tiny ones (adaptive thresholding). result: long-context p50 is +~10ms, p95 about the same. tradeoff seems acceptable for our SLOs.

sophia: can we please get the alert thresholds updated and a short blurb for release notes? support will get questions.

maya: updated SLO alert: p50 > 200ms and p95 > 500ms for production route, and added a canary panel. wrote a 1-paragraph note in the release doc.

aj: nice work. can we schedule a rollout plan to 100%? suggestions on how fast to ramp?

maya: ramping to 50% now and monitoring for 30m windows. if stable, we go to 100% in 3h. will watch GC, GPU util, and cache hit rates.

support-bot: @support alerted with summary: "Auto-prefix cache + adaptive batching canary metrics and rollout plan"

david: any config knobs we should expose to Dedicated customers or is this infra-only?

maya: infra-first. next step is an Optimize rule to recommend enabling this for compatible models. product + docs to follow.

sophia: can you add a small note for the console release banner so customers see potential latency/cost improvements?

maya: will do. follow-ups: 1) quantization + dynamic cache warmup experiments, 2) move adaptive thresholds to a traffic-aware policy, 3) add one more canary run for night traffic.

david: love it, great job team :tada:

maya: thanks all — ping me in thread if you spot anything odd.
